I don't have PTSD so I don't know if this will ultimately be useful, but... I have clinical depression, agoraphobia, and panic disorder. I ended up doing months of cognitive behavioral therapy with a neuropsychologist. I am not being dramatic in saying that it changed my life. At one point, I could not open my front door without a family member/friend with me. Now, I've finished a degree, have a job in a relatively stressful field, and use public transport almost daily.

It is hard work. I mentioned that it was months. However, the first month or two was intensive with 2-3 visits a week. Then it went to a weekly visit, then every two weeks, and so forth. And it is not to say that I never have problems. I still walk into stores and immediately walk out on occasion. I've have to get off Trimet more than once to have a cool down period. Overall, it was more than worth it to me.

Glad that you are recognizing the issue and getting help!

My sister has extremely severe social anxiety, basically PTSD without the post-tramatic part. The biggest help for her has been her service dog. Without the dog, she couldn't even leave the house without our mother, and would frequently have to come home from school. With the dog she could go more places, even on her own, and had to come home from school a lot less.

A service dog is something to look into, but be aware that your insurance will likely not pay for any part, and the dogs are quite expensive, with a non-profit costing 12-18 grand. A place to start is Angel Service Dogs, located in Colorado Springs. They do help with fundraising.

One problem with the current scoring system is that it promotes easy media like images to the detriment of more demanding one like texts. As a result subs often get dominated by image posts, and subs either have to impose special rules or split, like /r/gaming and /r/games on reddit.

The fundamental reason behind this is that some media are more immediately accessible than others, it's a psychological thing that cannot be changed.

A potential solution, besides the usual split of subs, would be to score differently images, videos and texts, such that an upvoat on an image would contribute less to its ranking than on a text contribution. The weights would be Images < Videos < Texts and could be tweaked to obtain the desirable mix of media.
